transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-16
Start time: 09:30 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah, Marcus Lee, Ellen Zhao (Redwood) — Samir Patel, Nina Gomez, Oliver Reed, Tara Kim (AlderBridge)

Auto-summary: Runbook review, security handoff, pilot scheduling, and benchmark prep.

-- Transcript (imperfect speech-to-text, timestamps approx) --
[00:00:05] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Priya with Redwood — I think you all have the runbook we shared, we'll run through the high level and then hand over ops tasks, how's that sound?
[00:00:18] Samir Patel: Yep that works, thanks Priya. Quick note, our timeline is tight — we want pilot in prod-ish env by end of month if feasible.
[00:00:28] Marcus Lee: Understood. We'll confirm feasibility after the benchmark. Ellen and I will own the test plan.
[00:00:36] Ellen Zhao: Morning — I'll cover the benchmark details and what we need from your side.
[00:00:42] Nina Gomez: Also want to flag networking — we have strict egress rules and we run a transit gateway, so we'll need the VPC/peering section clarified.
[00:00:52] Priya Shah: Absolutely, Nina. We'll go through the exact firewall ports and CIDR ranges in the runbook section.
[00:01:05] Oliver Reed: Can we also talk about model pinning and rollback? We need to ensure we don't accidentally flip to a higher-cost variant.
[00:01:12] Ellen Zhao: Yes — we support model pinning per route and can set automatic fallback to a lower-capacity variant if a rollout fails, that's in the rollout playbook.
[00:01:24] Tara Kim: On the security side, we're SOC 2 in process; main asks are: KMS integration (we use HashiCorp Vault), audit log retention 1 year, and SSO via Okta.
[00:01:36] Marcus Lee: Good notes. We have a Vault/KMS guide, and our audit logs can be exported to your SIEM — retention configurable. Okta SAML is supported, we'll include an SSO runbook.
[00:01:49] Samir Patel: What's the behavior on KV cache when we scale nodes? Curious about cold-start token cost.
[00:01:56] Ellen Zhao: The KV cache follows session affinity across a pod pool; on scale up there will be cold-cache misses for some keys, we'll show mitigation in the benchmark with warmed prefixes.
[00:02:12] [00:02:12] Speaker 5: (mumble) — sorry, go ahead.
[00:02:18] Priya Shah: No worries. Okay let's step through the runbook file — Marcus?
[00:02:24] Marcus Lee: Slide 1: Pre-activation checklist — network, DNS, SSO, KMS, and consent on PII handling. Slide 2: Pilot model list and success criteria. I'll read the list: "chat assistant v1 (open-model), semantic embeddings v2".
[00:02:45] Oliver Reed: For the chat assistant we need latency under 450ms p95 for 512 tokens, otherwise users complain. Is that realistic?
[00:02:54] Ellen Zhao: On hosted infra we can usually hit that with light batching and optimized kernels; if not, Dedicated pools reduce variance but add cost. We'll present tradeoffs.
[00:03:10] Nina Gomez: What's the unit charge on RDC tokens? We need ballpark for budgeting.
[00:03:15] Priya Shah: We'll send formal pricing, but expect per-token usage plus embedding unit fees. Marcus will attach a sample cost model for your expected QPS.
[00:03:26] Samir Patel: Ok. On the KMS front, does Redwood support customer-managed keys only via GCP/AWS KMS or Vault as well?
[00:03:33] Marcus Lee: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM partners; Vault can be integrated but requires an on-prem/private deployment flow — we'll capture the exact steps in the security pack.
[00:03:49] Tara Kim: We'll need that documented — we have regulatory constraints around key custody.
[00:03:54] Priya Shah: Noted. Action: Tara to send required custody matrix and we'll map to deployment options.
[00:04:02] [00:04:02] Ellen Zhao: Benchmark plan: We request a 2-hour reserved slot where we exercise 1–100 QPS ramp, include typical prompt mixes. We'll provide a load script and expected distributions. We'll also run a cache-warm run to show cold vs warm behavior.
[00:04:21] Nina Gomez: We'll need to run it in a staging VPC that mirrors prod — we can give you ephemeral peering.
[00:04:28] Ellen Zhao: Perfect, please share CIDR and the peering window.
[00:04:34] Oliver Reed: What's the expected output of the benchmark? SLA graph? Logs?
[00:04:38] Ellen Zhao: We'll provide latency percentiles, throughput, token cost estimates, and a short runbook of tuning knobs we applied.
[00:04:47] Marcus Lee: Also will include a short quality check — sample prompts and model outputs — to verify no regressions.
[00:04:54] Samir Patel: Great. On the onboarding timeline: if benchmark next week looks good, can we go to limited prod the following week?
[00:05:02] Priya Shah: Yes that's the usual cadence — benchmark, pilot, small prod ramp. We should set a go/no-go on 2026-02-24.
[00:05:10] Tara Kim: About logs and PII: do you redact automatically or is that customer responsibility?
[00:05:16] Marcus Lee: By default we store request/response in encrypted logs; redaction is a joint responsibility — we can enable request-side filters and also provide tooling to redact at ingestion. We'll document the options.
[00:05:30] Nina Gomez: For network ports: do you need outbound 443 only?
[00:05:34] Ellen Zhao: Outbound TLS to our endpoints over 443, plus a few management ports for the control plane — we'll list them precisely.
[00:05:44] [00:05:44] Speaker 3: (overlap) — also RBAC?
[00:05:47] Marcus Lee: Yes, RBAC via SCIM and Okta groups supported; we'll map roles to Redwood Console permissions.
[00:05:55] Oliver Reed: One more thing — can we pin model versions per route and have canary traffic?
[00:06:00] Ellen Zhao: Yes, canary rollouts and percent traffic splits are supported. We'll walk you through the console demo in the next call.
[00:06:08] Priya Shah: Let's look at the RACI in the runbook: who on the AlderBridge side will own networking and who will sign off on go-live?
[00:06:17] Samir Patel: Nina will own networking, Tara owns security sign-off, Samir will approve go.
[00:06:23] Marcus Lee: Noted — I'll add that to the runbook and send an updated copy.
[00:06:29] [00:06:29] Ellen Zhao: Quick doc refs: I'll post the benchmark script, a small terraform snippet for peering, and the SSO steps in the shared drive.
[00:06:39] Tara Kim: For the audit logs, can you push logs to our S3 with KMS-managed keys?
[00:06:45] Marcus Lee: Yes, we can export logs to your S3 bucket and encrypt with your KMS key; we'll need bucket policy details.
[00:06:53] Samir Patel: Anything else on legal / procurement? Oliver?
[00:06:57] Oliver Reed: Procurement is ready to review standard enterprise T&Cs; procurement asked for a copy of SOC2 report and a data processing addendum.
[00:07:06] Priya Shah: We'll send the SOC2 redacted report and the DPA; Marcus will attach the security pack.
[00:07:13] [00:07:13] Speaker 2: (brief) — okay sounds good.
[00:07:17] Marcus Lee: To recap next steps: Marcus will share updated runbook and cost model; Ellen will schedule the benchmark and share the load script; Tara and Nina will provide network and KMS details; Priya will circulate SOC2 and DPA. Follow-up meeting 2026-02-24 for go/no-go.
[00:07:35] Samir Patel: Good — thanks everyone.
[00:07:37] Priya Shah: Thanks all, we'll send notes and action items after this call.
[00:07:42] [End of call]
